items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: Joe Howard showed me a whole lot of stuff on trumpet. And gave me a whole lot of musical ideas.

ctx.x: Joe Howard used to be a trumpet player, but tell me he got on bass. But I can say this. Before I left here, Joe Howard showed me a whole lot of stuff on trumpet. And gave me a whole lot of musical ideas. He was a mighty fine man, boy. And to tell me he plays tuba now, I don't know. He's dead. Since I've been back. Why does he live? I want to. He's dead. He's dead. No, I didn't know that. I didn't know that.
Well, did you ever work with Old Man Allen's brass band?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: And Joe Howard. And when I first went to Chicago, who a lot of them fellas was playing that way?

ctx.x: And when I first went to Chicago, who a lot of them fellas was playing that way? Yeah, who a lot of them? That's how Lewis got such a jump on them. Even them two Smith brothers, they wasn't playing no good more than stuff in the time.
